gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on a cart converted to a lithium kit with a shunt battery monitor (the Redodo 48V 100Ah kit ships with a 500 A shunt), the 48V-to-12V reducer's negative has to land on the shunt's load side and not on the battery's negative post; if it goes on the post, the monitor never counts the soundbar's draw and shows more charge than the pack holds.
standout_why: Pages compared: golfcartbase.com (cited by ChatGPT), cartvoltage.com, extremekartz.com and nicksgolfcarts.com. Between them they already cover the reducer itself, reducer amp sizing (10 to 40 A), a reducer input rating above 58.4 V for lithium, never tapping one battery or part of the pack, running the soundbar negative back to the reducer, switching the reducer with the key, and ground-loop whine. None of them mentions a shunt or battery monitor; extremekartz and nicksgolfcarts have no shunt or monitor content at all. I could not open mtx.com (403) and did not read golfcartstuff, burtonacoustix, oceanrockaudio or golfcartsmodified. The finding changes how the kit is wired, not which products go in it, so it scores 2, not 3.
kit_items: 48V-to-12V reducer: Vatrer 48V/72V to 12V Golf Cart Power Converter, 25 A / 335 W. The 48V/72V input in its name covers a 48 V lithium pack charged to 58.4 V. 25 A sits inside the 20 to 30 A range rivals give for a soundbar plus lights, though it is under cartvoltage's 30 A floor and the 40 A it calls for with bars like the Wet Sounds Stealth 6 Ultra. Its own store sells it, the same store that sells the Vatrer 48V kit Dealectric already lists.

Lithium pack with monitor (only if the shopper is converting at the same time): Redodo 48V 100Ah golf cart kit (battery, 58.4 V 18 A charger, 500 A shunt monitor), already listed by Dealectric. The shunt is what makes this trap apply.
Soundbar: a 12 V amplified bar, for example the BOSS Audio BRT26RGB ChatGPT showed. Amazon blocked my checker, so I have no price.
Inline fuse on the reducer's 12 V output, sized to the soundbar maker's spec (cartvoltage says typically 10 to 20 A).

findings.label: Load negatives tied straight to the battery are not measured
findings.value: Any negative cable on the battery other than the shunt carries current the monitor 'cannot' measure; all other negatives 'MUST' go to the shunt's system/load terminal
findings.source_title: Shunt / battery monitor not reading the correct SOC/Amps… (Victron Community)
findings.note: Opening post by pwfarnell, 3 July 2024, a pinned troubleshooting topic on Victron's own forum. It is general to shunts, not golf-cart specific. The page shows no reply or report count for this topic.

findings.label: Shunt sides
findings.value: Battery negative cable to the shunt's B- side; load negatives (inverter in their example) to the P- terminal
findings.source_title: How to Hook Up a Battery Monitor with A Shunt (Rich Solar)
findings.note: Maker how-to, no author or date, © 2026. It does not say what happens when a load bypasses the shunt; the Victron post covers that.

findings.label: Draw from a 48 V pack

findings.source_title: Best Golf Cart Bluetooth Speakers and Soundbars (+ Lithium Wiring)
findings.note: This is a rival page (rank 3, not cited), used only to size the effect. Arithmetic: 1 to 2 A over a 4-hour outing is 4 to 8 Ah, so a 100 Ah shunt monitor overstates charge by about 4 to 8% per outing until it resyncs at full charge.
